To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the generalisation error of generalised linear models in the lazy training paradigm can be computed analytically using the replica method; (ii) the generalisation performance in this regime is determined by the geometry of the data manifold and its correlations; (iii) the double descent phenomenon in generalisation performance can be analytically explained by the geometry of data manifold and its intrinsic dimension; (iv) random projections are not always the best choice for learning with random features.

(i) we derive the generalisation performance of generalised linear regression in the high dimensional regime, for a large class of loss functions and in both the under- and over-parametrised regimes; and (ii) we show that in this regime, generalised linear regression with random features can perform as well as deep networks, provided that the random features are orthogonal.

1) we provide a closed-form expression for the generalisation error in learning random features in the under-parametrised regime and in the lazy training of neural networks; 2) we provide a new perspective on learning in the hidden manifold model; 3) we show that orthogonal projections are better than random ones for learning with random features; 4) we show that the generalisation error is a non-decreasing function of the correlation in the data generated from the hidden manifold model.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have provided a general theoretical framework to study generalisation error in the over parametrised regime of a large class of machine learning algorithms, and that we have used it to provide analytical results for a broad class of learning scenarios.

, by studying the generalised linear regression problem in a high dimensional setting, we have obtained an analytical expression for the generalisation performance of a large family of learning algorithms, and we have shown how the asymptotic performance of these algorithms depends on the data generation mechanism.

we are able to obtain a closed form expression of the generalisation error for a large class of models and loss functions, which is valid in the under and over parameterised regimes, and for different types of data distributions, including those with correlations.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the generalisation performance in learning with random projections is governed by a single quantity, the overlap between the random projections and a hidden manifold in the input space, which can be computed exactly for a large class of models.
the replica method can be used to obtain a complete analytical characterisation of the generalisation error for a broad range of learning tasks.

, by using the replica method, it is possible to study the generalisation performance in high dimensional problems with a broad class of models in a closed and analytical way, without the need to rely on the asymptotic regime of infinite data or on the assumption of Gaussianity.
